profile.stagger_pattern: No stagger. Mayor, Vice Mayor, 5 at-large and 35 district seats all elected concurrently in the August general of odd years (2019, 2023, 2027), with a September runoff for any seat where no candidate takes a majority. All 42 offices turn over on the same date.

run_log.detail: Registry entry for Nashville confirmed correct on all three points: the city's own results archive at nashville.gov/departments/elections/... is live and reaches back to 2008; the Metro Council is still 40 members (35 district + 5 at-large) - the 2023 state reduction law never took effect; nashville.legistar.com is live. sos.tn.gov / elections.tn.gov were not needed and not tested. Registry path 'nashville.gov/departments/elections/election-results' 404s; the working path is '/departments/elections/election-results-and-statistics/election-results'.

Full election archive index enumerated by curl from the results page: it lists EVERY Davidson County election 2008-2026. Between 2019 and 2026 the only Metro Council contests are the Feb 12 / Mar 19 2019 District 29 special, the Aug 1 / Sep 12 2019 metro general+runoff, and the Aug 3 / Sep 14 2023 metro general+runoff. There was NO Davidson County election of any kind in 2021. This index is the decisive negative evidence for the mid-term check (see below).

All six cycle result pages fetched (HTTP 200, titled 'Certified'). The per-contest results are rendered client-side, so candidate-level vote tables were not extracted; the pages are used as cycle sources and the seated composition comes from the ACFR series instead.

ACFR route (cross-state finding 3c) is the spine for this city and worked perfectly. Metro Nashville publishes a true ACFR with an 'ELECTED OFFICIALS / Members of the Metropolitan Council' page dated 'at June 30, YYYY', naming the Mayor, the Vice Mayor, all 5 at-large and all 35 district members. Seven consecutive reports FY2019-FY2025 downloaded by curl and read with pdftotext -layout - one verbatim annual snapshot for every panel year through 2025. Diffing consecutive years is what located the mid-term changes.

THREE mid-term events found, all dated. (1) At-large member Steve Glover RESIGNED effective 2022-03-01 (health); Metro Charter leaves an at-large vacancy unfilled until the next general election, so the seat stayed VACANT 2022-03-01 to 2023-10-01 - independently confirmed by the FY2022 and FY2023 ACFRs, which both print 'At Large  Vacant', and by Legistar, which labels his person record 'Steve Glover (resigned 3/1/2022)'. (2) District 29: Karen Johnson resigned 2018-08-31; special election 2019-02-12 with runoff 2019-03-19 seated Delishia Porterfield, so D29 was vacant from 2019-01-01 to 2019-03-19. (3) At-Large 5 was already vacant entering the window: Jim Shulman left his at-large seat on winning the September 2018 Vice Mayor special, and the FY2019 ACFR confirms 'Vacant' at 2019-06-30; that seat stayed vacant until 2019-10-01. NEGATIVE RESULT, well-evidenced: the complete election archive shows no Metro Council special election at any date 2020-2026. Because Nashville must fill a DISTRICT vacancy by special election whenever more than eight months remain in the term, the absence of any special election - combined with seven annual ACFR snapshots plus the current Legistar roster all showing 35 named district members - means no district seat turned over mid-term anywhere in 2019-2026. The 2023-2027 term has had zero vacancies through August 2026.

Seat count verified at 42 elective offices (Mayor + separately elected Vice Mayor + 5 at-large + 35 district) and CONSTANT across the whole window - the 2023 state law cutting the council to 20 was enjoined and never took effect, and none of the seven ACFRs shows a size change. Vice Mayor recorded as role 'vice_mayor' with stable seat_label 'Vice Mayor': it is a real at-large elected seat that presides over the Council, per the ACFR narrative ('The Charter also provides for a Vice Mayor, who is elected at large for a four-year term and is the presiding officer of the Metropolitan Council'). 2026 coverage cross-checked against the live Legistar people list (https://nashville.legistar.com/People.aspx), which returns exactly 42 active records matching the FY2025 ACFR name-for-name (Joy Smith Kimbrough=Joy Kimbrough, Jennifer Webb=Jennifer Frensley Webb, Bob Nash=Robert Nash), so nothing changed between 2025-06-30 and 2026-08. DAY-OF-WEEK CHECK: a search summary claimed the public inauguration date 2023-10-01 was 'a Saturday' - it was a Sunday; the private swearing-in 2023-09-25 was correctly a Monday, matching the Nashville Banner's dated story. BOUNDARY CONVENTION: mayor's start recorded as the sourced private swearing-in 2023-09-25; Vice Mayor and all 40 council seats recorded as 2023-10-01 (public inauguration). The 2019 handover is recorded uniformly at 2019-10-01; the exact 2019 swearing-in day was not separately sourced, which shifts no seat-year. SEAT-LABEL CAVEAT: Nashville's five at-large seats are legally undifferentiated - they are filled by a single five-winner at-large race and carry no ballot numbers. 'At-Large 1'..'At-Large 5' are therefore ANALYTIC labels assigned here by person-continuity across terms so each label forms one unbroken chain (At-Large 5 = Shulman-vacancy -> Glover -> vacancy -> Evans Segall). They are stable within this file but are not official designations. TRUNCATION NOTE: the 2015-elected members' rows start at 2019-01-01 because their real term start (October 2015) precedes the panel window; entry_mode is 'unknown' for those rows rather than asserting an unsourced cycle.

42 seats x 8 years = 336 seat-years, all covered by a tenure row. No gaps filed: the three vacancies found are all PARTIAL-year (2019 D29 Jan-Mar; 2019 At-Large 5 Jan-Sep; 2022 At-Large 5 Mar-Dec and 2023 Jan-Sep), so every affected seat-year also has a sourced holder and none qualifies as a vacant seat-year under the brief's rule.
